<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="an-existing-platform"><a href="#an-existing-platform">An existing platform</a></h2>

MLAI-CORPORATION-WWW already exists. At the reviewed revision, apps/web contains the Quesar by MLAI website, while apps/mobile and apps/quasar have their own responsibilities and verification flows. The original greenfield assertion was incorrect.

The active web application is a Next.js TypeScript/TSX surface. Its README explicitly rejects reviving the old Vite, Hono, and Rust/Axum migration directions. This review does not modify or replace that app.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="separate-verification-boundaries"><a href="#separate-verification-boundaries">Separate verification boundaries</a></h2>

The repository retains app-specific lockfiles and check commands. A green web gate is not mobile evidence, a mobile export is not a signed device run, and a site-builder unit test is not a live provider generation.

<CodeBlock code={"bun run check:topology\nbun run check:web"} note={"Run these only in the existing MLAI platform checkout after its documented setup. They are not this preview’s commands."} />

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="this-review-build"><a href="#this-review-build">This review build</a></h2>

This deliverable includes a self-contained review website and an isolated Next.js/React source candidate. The review is exported from shared TSX markup without installing Next or React; its browser checks do not verify framework hydration, bundling, or Fumadocs integration.

The Next source uses a small interactive boundary and Fumadocs MDX content loading. Dependency installation, a lockfile, full type-checking, the framework build, and deployment remain explicit integration gates. Nothing here changes production, DNS, credentials, or a GitHub branch.

</section>
